findings.comment: -Inspector observed the top of the dish machine to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC. findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: The facility was observed to have the order sheet from Kellner showing that they did order the test strips, however, after inspecting the shipment and putting it away, no test strips were observed with the delivery. During the inspection, the PIC texted the delivery driver with Kellner. With no response from the delivery driver during today’s inspection, an additional follow-up will take place after Christmas break. After discussion with the PIC, the follow-up will take place on Tuesday, January 9th, 2024.
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
A certified food protection manager (CFPM) must be present during hours of operation.  Along with the CFPM certification, an allergen awareness training certification must also be obtained for all high risk facilities.  Ensure the kitchen manager obtains these certifications.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
At time of inspection, the sanitizer bucket had a concentration of 0 ppm (q).  Discussed with PIC, who stated that she also adds Dawn dish soap to the sanitizer.  Inspector advised PIC to not add soap to sanitizer as it affects the sanitizer concentration.  COS

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Heat sanitation is used in the dish machine, no chemical sanitizer is used.   No temperature measuring device is available to measure the temperature in the dish machine.  PIC was informed a temperature measuring device is required. Ensure a measuring device is present and readily available.

4-204.115: A WAREWASHING machine shall be equipped with a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE that indicates the temperature of the water

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Non contact food surfaces were observed to contain dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris:  box fan used in the kitchen for staff, fan in the walk in cooler and spray nozzle over dish area. The dust could cause cross contamination on food and non food contact surfaces.  Ensure fan blades are cleaned regularly to prevent the build up debris.  Spray nozzle over dish sink was observed to contain food debris.  Ensure spray nozzle, handle, and spray head are cleaned regularly to prevent cross contamination.

601.11: (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-202.11  (P ) Plumbing is not designed , constructed and installed properly. Contact a licensed plumber to repair/replace to comply with Illinois Plumbing Code. 
When someone is using the spray hose to wash dishes, the handsink has about 10 seconds of flow and then stops. Inspector was trying to wash hands at start of inspection, while an employee was washing dishes, and was unable to complete handwashing until employee was done washing the dish. The handwashing sink does work properly as long as the spray hose in the dish area is not in use. The Handwashing Sink must be available without interruption at all times in the kitchen, not hindered by the use of other equipment. Follow up to occur Thursday 2/13/2020 to correct the issue. Contact a licensed plumber to repair connection to handsink and dish area.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Improper handwashing technique was observed. Faucet was shut off without barrier to drying hands with paper towels. Kitchen staff were advised on proper technique (have paper towels ready, dry hands after washing is completed, then use paper towels as a barrier to shut off manual faucet). Hands were re-washed using proper technique.

Hands must be properly washed any time they may have been contaminated and before working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Mouse droppings were found in dry store room in the following places:
(a) on white floor ledge along entry wall (behind rolling barrels), 
(b) on white floor ledge behind rolling green hot box, 
(c) in muffin tins and baking sheets to right of rolling green hot box (on shelves),

750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

Bucket of chlorine sanitizer and wet wiping cloths measured 0-10ppm chlorine.  CORRECTED - bucket was immediately re-made and measured at 100ppm.  Make sure to monitor sanitizing buckets for decrease in sanitizer concentration and change solution frequently.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Mouse droppings were found in dry store room in the following places:
(a) along entry wall (behind rolling barrels), 
(b) in the corner behind the rolling green hot box, 
(c) in the corner near the rolling barrels and under the hanging sacks, 
(d, under the electrical panel, near hot water heater, outside the dry storage "cage", and
e, to the left of the washing machine (boiler room).
The 10/28/13 inspection report states that there is no evidence of pest activity in dry store room or boiler room.  These mouse droppings appear to indicate new mouse activity.  Orkin reports were reviewed (see General Comments).  Eliminate all mouse droppings and monitor for further activity.  All food & equipment is well-protected from pests.
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.
